# TPM auth method (API)

<EnterpriseAlert product="vault" />

This is the API documentation for the Vault TPM authentication method. The TPM
auth method allows clients that hold a TPM (Trusted Platform Module) device to
authenticate using TLS client certificates backed by hardware attestation.

Before a TPM can authenticate, it must be enrolled via the [`identity/tpm`](/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/tpm#create-a-tpm) endpoint
in the same namespace as the TPM auth method is mounted in, and the TPM
auth method must be configured with at least one role.

This documentation assumes the TPM auth method is mounted at the `/auth/tpm`
path in Vault. Since it is possible to enable auth methods at any location,
please update your API calls accordingly.

---

## Configure

Set the internal CA parameters for the TPM auth backend. The backend manages
its own CA that it uses to issue and verify client certificates. Writing to
this endpoint on first use initialises the CA; subsequent writes update the
CA rotation parameters and may rotate the active CA if the new settings
require it.

| Method | Path              |
| :----- | :---------------- |
| `POST` | `/auth/tpm/config` |

### Parameters

- `ca_lifetime` `(duration: "8760h")` – How long each CA certificate is valid
  once it becomes the active CA. The backend always pre-generates a *Next* CA
  before the *Active* CA expires, so there is no gap in signing capability.
  Accepts a Go duration string (e.g. `"8760h"`, `"365d"`) or an integer number
  of seconds.

- `ca_soft_expiry` `(duration: "720h")` – How long before the hard expiry of
  the Active CA it stops signing new certificates. When the Active CA's
  remaining lifetime drops below this window it is retired and the pre-generated
  Next CA is promoted. Must be less than `ca_lifetime / 2`. Accepts a Go
  duration string or an integer number of seconds.

- `default_cert_ttl` `(duration: "")` – Default lifetime for client
  certificates issued by the [`gentpmcert`](#begin-tpm-certificate-issuance)
  endpoint when the role does not specify `cert_ttl`. When unset or `0`, the
  effective TTL falls back to `ca_soft_expiry`. The actual certificate lifetime
  is always capped by the signing CA's remaining validity.

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "ca_lifetime": "8760h",
  "ca_soft_expiry": "720h",
  "default_cert_ttl": "168h"
}
```

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ..." \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/tpm/config
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "ca_lifetime": "8760h0m0s",
    "ca_soft_expiry": "720h0m0s",
    "default_cert_ttl": "168h0m0s"
  }
}
```

## Create or update role

Creates or updates a named role. Roles define which TPM devices (by individual
ID or by group membership) may obtain client certificates and authenticate
against this mount, and also govern the Vault token parameters issued on
successful login.

At least one of `tpm_ids` or `tpmgroup_ids` is required.

| Method | Path                  |
| :----- | :-------------------- |
| `POST` | `/auth/tpm/role/:name` |

### Parameters

- `name` `(string: <required>)` – Name of the role. Used in API paths and
  stored in lower-case.

- `tpm_ids` `(array: [] or comma-delimited string: "")` – List of TPM record
  IDs (EK SHA-256 hashes in the form `sha256-<hex>`) that are authorized to
  use this role. TPMs are enrolled via the
  [`identity/tpm`](/vault/api-docs/secret/identity/tpm#create-a-tpm) endpoint.

- `tpmgroup_ids` `(array: [] or comma-delimited string: "")` – List of TPM
  group IDs whose members are authorised to use this role. Group membership is
  evaluated at login time.

- `display_name` `(string: "")` – The display name attached to tokens issued
  when authenticating with this role. Defaults to the role name if not set.

- `cert_ttl` `(duration: "")` – Lifetime for client certificates issued by the
  [`gentpmcert`](#begin-tpm-certificate-issuance) endpoint for this role. Zero
  means inherit the global `default_cert_ttl` from config, falling back to
  `ca_soft_expiry`. Accepts a Go duration string or an integer number of
  seconds.

@include 'tokenfields.mdx'

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "tpm_ids": ["sha256-abc123..."],
  "display_name": "my-device",
  "token_ttl": "1h",
  "token_policies": ["default", "my-policy"]
}
```

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ..." \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/tpm/role/my-role
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "name": "my-role",
    "display_name": "my-device",
    "tpm_ids": ["sha256-abc123..."],
    "tpmgroup_ids": [],
    "cert_ttl": 0,
    "token_ttl": 3600,
    "token_max_ttl": 0,
    "token_policies": ["default", "my-policy"]
  }
}
```

## Begin TPM certificate issuance

Phase 1 of the two-phase TPM attestation protocol. The client submits its
Endorsement Key (EK) public key and Attestation Key (AK) parameters. Vault
verifies that the EK corresponds to a TPM enrolled under the given role, then
generates an encrypted credential challenge using the EK.

This endpoint is **unauthenticated** — no Vault token is required.

| Method | Path                                    |
| :----- | :-------------------------------------- |
| `POST` | `/auth/tpm/role/:role_name/gentpmcert/begin` |

### Parameters

- `role_name` `(string: <required>)` – Name of the role to issue a certificate
  for.

- `ek_public_key` `(string: <required>)` – PEM-encoded RSA or EC public key
  for the TPM's Endorsement Key. The TPM ID is derived as
  `sha256-<hex(SHA-256(DER bytes))>` and matched against the enrolled TPM
  records.

- `ak_params` `(string: <required>)` – Base64-encoded JSON object containing
  the Attestation Key's TPM 2.0 public parameters. The object has the following
  fields:

  | Field | Type | Description |
  | :---- | :--- | :---------- |
  | `public` | `bytes` | AK canonical encoding (TPM2B\_PUBLIC / TPMT\_PUBLIC). |
  | `create_data` | `bytes` | TPMS\_CREATION\_DATA structure for the AK. |
  | `create_attestation` | `bytes` | TPMS\_ATTEST structure for the AK. |
  | `create_signature` | `bytes` | TPMT\_SIGNATURE over `create_attestation`. |
  | `use_tcsd_activation_format` | `bool` | Set when the trousers daemon (tcsd) is used. |

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/tpm/role/my-role/gentpmcert/begin
```

### Sample response

The `encrypted_credentials` value is a base64-encoded JSON blob containing a
TPM2 `EncryptedCredential` structure. The client must pass it to the TPM's
`TPM2_ActivateCredential` command using the AK handle and the EK handle; the
TPM returns the raw secret bytes if and only if the AK was created on the same
TPM as the EK.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "challenge_id": "dGVzdGNoYWxsZW5nZQ==",
    "encrypted_credentials": "base64-encoded-credential-blob..."
  }
}
```

The challenge expires after **5 minutes**. At most one outstanding challenge
per TPM is kept; submitting a new `/begin` request for the same EK invalidates
any previous challenge. Requests from the same EK are rate-limited to one every
10 seconds.

---

## Finish TPM certificate issuance

Phase 2 of the two-phase TPM attestation protocol. The client submits the
decrypted challenge response (proving hardware possession) along with a CSR and
key certification parameters (proving the application key was created on the
same TPM). Vault verifies all inputs and, if successful, issues a client
certificate signed by the backend's active CA.

This endpoint is **unauthenticated** — no Vault token is required.

| Method | Path                                     |
| :----- | :--------------------------------------- |
| `POST` | `/auth/tpm/role/:role_name/gentpmcert/finish` |

### Parameters

- `role_name` `(string: <required>)` – Name of the role the certificate is
  being issued for. Must match the role supplied to `/begin`.

- `ek_public_key` `(string: <required>)` – PEM-encoded EK public key.  Must
  match the key used in the corresponding `/begin` call.

- `challenge_id` `(string: <required>)` – The `challenge_id` value returned by
  the `/begin` call.

- `challenge_response` `(string: <required>)` – Base64-encoded raw bytes
  returned by the TPM's `TPM2_ActivateCredential` command. Must equal the
  secret generated during `/begin`.

- `csr` `(string: <required>)` – PEM-encoded PKCS#10 Certificate Signing
  Request for the application key. The key in the CSR must be TPM-resident (see
  `key_certification`).

- `key_certification` `(string: <required>)` – Base64-encoded JSON object
  containing the TPM certification parameters that prove the application key
  (matching the CSR) was created inside the same TPM. The object has the
  following fields:

  | Field | Type | Description |
  | :---- | :--- | :---------- |
  | `public` | `bytes` | Application key canonical encoding (TPMT\_PUBLIC). |
  | `create_data` | `bytes` | TPMS\_CREATION\_DATA structure for the key. |
  | `create_attestation` | `bytes` | TPMS\_ATTEST structure for the key. |
  | `create_signature` | `bytes` | TPMT\_SIGNATURE over `create_attestation`, signed by the AK. |

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    https://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/auth/tpm/role/my-role/gentpmcert/finish
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "ca_chain": [
      "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    ]
  }
}
```

The issued certificate embeds two OtherName SAN extensions:

| OID suffix | Value |
| :--------- | :---- |
| `1.3.6.1.4.1.55813.1.1.1` | TPM ID (`sha256-<hex>`) derived from the EK public key. |
| `1.3.6.1.4.1.55813.1.1.2` | Role name used during issuance. |

Both values are verified at login time.

---

## Login

Authenticate using a TPM-backed client certificate obtained from the
[`gentpmcert`](#begin-tpm-certificate-issuance) endpoints. The certificate
must be presented as the TLS client certificate on the connection; Vault
verifies the chain against its internal CA, checks the TPM ID and role-name
OtherName SANs, confirms the TPM is enrolled, and checks role authorisation
before issuing a token.

This endpoint is **unauthenticated** — no Vault token is required.

| Method | Path              |jjjjjjjjjjjjjjj
| :----- | :---------------- |
| `POST` | `/auth/tpm/login` |

### Parameters

- `role_name` `(string: <required>)` – The name of the role to authenticate
  against. Must match the role name embedded in the client certificate's
  OtherName SAN.

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "role_name": "my-role"
}
```

### Sample request

There is no mechanism in curl to use a TPM-embedded private key, so instead here's how to do it with the Vault cli:

```bash
vault login -method=cert -tpm-state-dir=/private -role_name=my-role
```


### Sample response

```json
{
  "auth": {
    "client_token": "cf95f87d-f95b-47ff-b1f5-ba7bff850425",
    "policies": ["default", "my-policy"],
    "metadata": {
      "role_name": "my-role",
      "common_name": "tpm-client",
      "serial_number": "123456789",
      "subject_key_id": "aa:bb:cc:...",
      "authority_key_id": "dd:ee:ff:...",
      "tpm_id": "sha256-abc123..."
    },
    "lease_duration": 3600,
    "renewable": true
  }
}
```

The token alias name is set to the TPM ID (`sha256-<hex>`), which allows
consistent entity mapping across certificate rotations.
